Container.Name: plex-dbrepair
Container.Overview: Plex DBRepair is a one-shot Plex database maintenance using ChuckPa DBRepair v26.10.00. Automatically discovers a running Plex Docker container through the host Docker socket, copies the DBRepair executable into it, stops the Plex Media Server process (while keeping the Docker container running where supported), performs the selected operation, then restarts the Plex container after success. No Plex appdata mount is needed in this repair container. Choose DBREPAIR_MODE (automatic, check, vacuum, repair, reindex, deflate, prune). If more than one Plex container is eligible, set PLEX_CONTAINER_NAME to the exact container name. Persistent logs are stored under /logs. Database backups are enabled by default for all modes except prune. CAUTION: This tool modifies Plex databases. Keep independently verified backups. Tested with LinuxServer Plex on a disposable installation; Binhex and Hotio compatibility is not yet verified. If the Plex process respawns, its container exits, or repair fails, the tool may stop without restarting Plex. Set this repair container's restart policy to No to avoid repeated repairs.
Container.Requires: YOU ARE ULTIMATELY RESPONSIBLE FOR YOUR DATA. Requires access to /var/run/docker.sock and one supported RUNNING Plex container. The Docker socket grants host-level administrative privileges. Verify backups before changing databases. No Plex appdata bind mount is required. Install as a one-shot container with restart policy No. Binhex and Hotio have not yet been tested and validated, but should still work

Config.Name: Maintenance Mode
Config.Description: automatic=upstream auto; check=integrity checks; vacuum=compact; repair=rebuild including FTS; reindex=rebuild indexes; deflate=compact only if needed; prune=PhotoTranscoder cleanup. Select one mode.

Config.Name: Plex Container Name
Config.Description: auto detects one eligible Plex container. If you have multiple Plex containers, enter the exact Docker container name shown by docker ps (example: plex). Do not enter a Docker image name here.

Config.Name: Enable Database Backups
Config.Description: Create timestamped cold database archives inside the TARGET Plex container at Plex Media Server/DBRepair-Backups; skipped for prune. Backups take disk space and are not automatically deleted.

Config.Name: Restart Plex After Success
Config.Description: Restart the target Plex Docker container after successful maintenance. On database errors the script intentionally does not auto-restart Plex.

Config.Name: Prune Days
Config.Description: For prune mode only: remove eligible PhotoTranscoder cached files older than this number of days.

Config.Name: Plex Container Match
Config.Description: Case-insensitive name substring used when Plex Container Name=auto. Image names containing plex are also considered. Candidates must contain the Plex database at the configured path.

Config.Name: Plex Internal Config Mount
Config.Description: Path INSIDE the target Plex container to its config mount, usually /config. This is NOT a host volume to mount to DBRepair.

Config.Name: Plex Internal Relative Path
Config.Description: Relative path inside the target Plex container's config directory. Leave at default unless that Plex installation differs.

Config.Name: Allow Process Shutdown Fallback
Config.Description: If upstream DBRepair stop cannot shut down Plex, allow SIGTERM to the Plex Media Server process. No forced Docker stop/offline repair fallback is implemented.

Config.Name: Maintenance Timeout Seconds
Config.Description: Maximum DBRepair operation duration in seconds. A failure or timeout requires reviewing the database before restarting Plex.

Config.Name: Plex Shutdown Timeout Seconds
Config.Description: Maximum seconds to wait for the Plex process to stop before aborting.

Config.Name: Persistent Repair Logs
Config.Description: Host folder for timestamped DBRepair execution logs. Docker logs also show output.

Config.Name: Host Docker Socket
Config.Description: REQUIRED: Docker host socket for discovering Plex and running docker inspect/exec/cp/restart. Grants this tool host-level Docker control.
